definition: Vacillate means to fluctuate or hesitate between choices.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word vacillate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know vacillate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: All autumn the farm vacillated between selling the herd and expanding it, buying feed one week and printing sale flyers the next.
To hedge is the mildest move — you avoid committing in words while standing still; it stops far short of vacillating.
To waver stops short of vacillating: wavering is one wobble of resolve, while vacillating swings you fully from side to side and back.

Seesaw is the picture word — scores, moods, and leads seesaw, tipping back and forth like the playground plank. It describes visible motion more than a mind at work. Vacillate is the formal word for a chooser: a voter, board, or buyer swinging between options that demand a decision.

To flip-flop is to reverse a stated position, usually in public — a candidate flip-flops when this week's speech contradicts last week's. Vacillate happens earlier and more privately: the mind swings between choices before any position is announced. Flip-flopping needs an audience; to vacillate needs only an unmade decision.
to land on one choice and stay there
to lock a decision in place
Vacillate comes from Latin vacillare, 'to sway or totter.' The -ate is a common verb ending, but the vacill- root appears in no other English word, so there is no cousin to point to.
Vacillate means to fluctuate or hesitate between choices.

Bree vacillated between the two wedding venues for months — booking the orchard in spring, switching to the ballroom when the forecast turned, then switching back — until both quietly gave her dates away.

Vacillate is more specific than 'waver': a waver is one wobble of resolve, while vacillating is a repeated swing between choices — committing first to one side, then the other, and landing on neither.
Vacillate is the formal word for swinging between positions — voters, boards, and buyers vacillate.
Its unit-mate dither fusses without ever choosing; vacillating chooses constantly, a different side each time.
For numbers that rise and fall, the word is fluctuate, not vacillate.

The 'For Sale' sign has been in and out of Grandma Ruth's yard so many times the realtor stopped charging to move it.
In June she is certain: the house is too big, the stairs too steep, the garden too much.
By August she is just as certain the opposite way, and the sign comes down again.
Her daughters have watched her vacillate for three years now, swinging whole-hearted from selling to staying, and they have learned not to schedule anything around either mood.
The realtor keeps the sign in his trunk.
